task.title: intword rounds a value just below a googol up to "1.0 googol"
task.body:
Why: https://github.com/python-humanize/humanize/issues/356 ; src/humanize/number.py:278-291 only carries between adjacent powers, but the powers list jumps from 10**33 to 10**100. On b519e48 `intword(10**100 - 10**93)` returns '9999999000000000610151082626636586748864734715312950532670947852288.0 decillion'.
Outcome: `humanize.intword(value, format="%.1f")` uses the googol unit for a positive or negative integer whose count in googols (`abs(value) / 10**100`), once formatted with `format`, reaches 1 or more: `intword(10**100 - 10**93) == '1.0 googol'`, `intword(10**100 - 10**98) == '1.0 googol'`, `intword(-(10**100 - 10**93)) == '-1.0 googol'`, `intword(10**100 - 10**93, format="%.0f") == '1 googol'`. The exact count is computed with integers, so the result does not depend on float rounding of the huge value. Unchanged: `intword(10**100) == '1.0 googol'`, `intword(10**33) == '1.0 decillion'`, `intword(10**36) == '1000.0 decillion'`, `intword(999_999_999) == '1.0 billion'`, `intword(1000) == '1.0 thousand'`. Values whose googol count stays below 1 after formatting (for example `10**50`) are left unspecified.
Proof: add tests to tests/test_number.py.

install: python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -q babel -e '.[tests]' && .venv/bin/pybabel --quiet compile --directory src/humanize/locale --domain humanize
